description: Central European deciduous forest — beech, oak, hornbeam under a closed canopy, with meadow clearings, creek valleys, and the ruins of the people who managed it for centuries. Rich, seasonal, and honest: the mast feeds you in fall, the gap starves you in spring.
hazards: wild boar (all year — sows with young)
name: Temperate European Forest

fall.note: Mast season. Acorns, beechnuts, hazel, mushrooms. Fatten up — the gap is coming.

spring.note: The hungry gap ends here — wild garlic, first greens. Ticks wake up too.

summer.note: Berries, mushrooms after rain, heat in the clearings. Boar are bold.

winter.note: The boss. Nuts and stored food or nothing. The wolves come closer.
